Priya / Kim / Jordan — attaching a quick model (see attachment: sablex_throughput_model_v1.xlsx). Summary first pass below. Assumptions: typical prompt 160 tokens in, 120 tokens out; p95 target 280ms; concurrency during bursts ~30 concurrent user streams (their burst note).

Model variants tested (quantized denotes int8 where applicable):
- model-A (standard, fp16, large context): 45 tokens/sec per A100-80GB (single stream, steady-state)
- model-A-quant (int8): 72 tokens/sec per A100-80GB (reduced memory pressure, slightly higher latency variance)
- model-A-lowlat (H100-optim, kernel-tuned): 95 tokens/sec per H100-80GB (optimized for small batches, best p95)

Mapping to slabs (round-trip numbers include caching warmup ~10% benefit for steady traffic):
- Conservative commit (production SLA, 20% headroom): 4 x A100-80GB dedicated = ~288 tokens/sec (using model-A-quant baseline) -> comfortably handles 30 tps bursts with room for growth to ~40 tps with autoscaling/burst lanes before degradation.
- Low-latency commit (if they require p95 <= 280ms strict): 2 x H100 + 2 x A100 hybrid (H100 for latency-critical streams, A100 for background/rerank) -> combined effective approx 260-300 tps for mixed workloads (note H100 licensing premium).
- Cost-minimized: 8 x T4-equivalent nodes (inference-optimized) ~120 tokens/sec — fits baseline but no headroom for bursts, not recommended for SLA-backed contract.

Canary/fallback plan:
1) Canary: start with 2 A100 slab + reserved burst pool (shared Dedicated burst capacity) — ramp to full commit after 2 weeks of traffic validation.
2) Fallback: automatic routing to quantized model-A-quant (lower quality delta <2% on our eval set) when slab utilization >85%.
3) Emergency global fallback to hosted multi-tenant low-latency model (graceful degradation, increased per-token charge) if sustained demand exceeds reserved + burst capacity.

Headroom & runway: recommend 20-25% committed headroom on day-one; plan a capacity review at month 1 and month 3 post-launch; include burst credits for the first 90 days to smooth onboarding spikes.

I'll attach the spreadsheet (detailed per-model TPS/tokens-per-second calc and latency calibration) and a short pdf SLO summary.

Ben
